purpose: Understand the normalization stage and validate fixed connection-gain scope before considering any fresh coding utility study.
model_scope: Only local random-weight Gemma4TextMLP and Gemma4RMSNorm modules. No pretrained checkpoint,decoder generation,task prompt or new neuron training.

analytical_probe.arithmetic: FP64 analytical reference; actual library RMSNorm uses FP32 internal arithmetic and casts to input dtype.
analytical_probe.equation: For R(y)=w*y/sqrt(mean(y^2)+eps),R(2y)/R(y)=sqrt((m+eps)/(m+eps/4)) elementwise where nonzero. Positive uniform scaling approximately cancels only when m dominates eps.
analytical_probe.theorem_check: FP64 formula relativeL2<=1e-12. No prescribed equality tolerance or universal numerical floor for the actual implementation. Report all differences.

coupling_probe.requirement: Only raw coordinate0 changes;actual normalization changes all three other output coordinates. This is a constructed arithmetic example,not a discovered pretrained neuron.

module_probe.weight_edits: Only declared down columns;each assignment followed by exact original-matrix restoration. Expected six total down-parameter version increments per dtype. All gate/up/norm versions and gradient flags unchanged;all p.grad None.
module_probe.comparison: Measure raw and normalized outputs for stored and activation forms,including hashes,maxabs/relativeL2. Do not assume exact equivalence or choose a form by numerical success.
module_probe.scope: Hooks apply to all three positions in a module forward and are removed. All outside edited columns remain byte-exact.

stopping: Any scope,restoration,hook/version,gradient or FP64 theorem check failure is preserved and stops interpretation. No pretrained model conclusion.
